summary.text: Visit an MOH-accredited assessor. You are likely severely disabled if you cannot do at least three daily activities.

details.heading: Daily activities assessed
details.body: The activities are bathing, dressing, feeding yourself, using the toilet, moving around and transferring.

details.heading: Examples of severe disability
details.body: You may be severely disabled if you need full help with at least three activities, such as eating, bathing, managing diapers or a catheter, dressing, moving, or transferring between a bed and chair.

steps.name: Visit an assessor
steps.text: Visit a MOH-accredited severe disability assessor to find out whether you are severely disabled.

example_phrasings: How do I know whether I have developed severe disability?
How can I tell if I am severely disabled?
Do I need help with three daily activities?

sources.page_title: How do I know whether I have developed severe disability?

quotes.text: You are likely to be assessed as severely disabled if you are unable to perform at least three Activities of Daily Living (ADLs).
You would need to visit a MOH-accredited severe disability assessor to be assessed whether you are severely disabled.
These ADLs are bathing, dressing, feeding oneself, using the toilet, moving around and transferring.
